dispositions.rationale: The case check refuses a validation record whose decision is not an acceptance.
The S2.6 continuation now requires the comparison to name no regressed case.
One sentence is the authoring form of the detection statement, which the judge reads whole; no scored behaviour depends on its sentence count.
The source revision is provenance; a harvested document is edited to plant its defect, so nothing in the tree can compare it with the revision, and the owner reads it at validation.
The installer suite holds test_eval_corpora_never_deploy_for_any_tool, which fails when any skill evals/ directory reaches a staging plan.
Same as behavioural-outcome-1; ACE-D2 names the owner as the acceptance authority at validation with the decision recorded.
ACE-D2: the owner confirms at validation that the planted defect is the one ACE-D3 names and that the control carries the no-finding feature; the decision is in the record the case check reads.
ACE-D6 Reads column now names a fresh context; ACE-A18 refuses a run whose isolation differs.
The judge identity the record can hold is its resolved model ID and prompt digest, which ACE-A20 checks; the invocation path is not observable in a committed record.
Recorded identifiers are attestations like the reports themselves; the tree cannot ask the transport what ran.
Fails at every other count.
Fails at every other count.
The planner plans a retest for every side at three of five.
P1 locks at four or five of five or eight to ten of ten after a retest, and at no other count.
Writing the plan before dispatch rests on the operator, as the decision states; nothing in the committed tree can observe it.
Committing every attempt rests on the operator, as the decision states; nothing in the committed tree can observe it.
A report lacking a response ID refuses the attempt.
The first entry is a constant the suite holds, the template digest at the commit S2.4 lands.
The lock sets an entry names must carry the entry digest and the one before it in their fingerprints.

S2.6 delivers body revisions and the comparison measures their effect; a case locked without a mandate is what the comparison is for, and a rule text absent from a lens body is what the rule-ownership suite checks.
Same as behavioural-outcome-2.
The verification child is a tracker item the human closes under ACQ-D2; the tree cannot observe the tracker.
The gate clause in a continuation line is the delivery contract gate the work facade requires there, not a criterion of this spec.
ACE-D7: each lens run inside a P1 panel run enters its own lens pool and is empty when that lens reported empty.
ACE-D8: the planner writes a retest extension before the retest; usable reports match the planned runs of the attempt and its retest.
An absent calibration record refuses the task.
A record calibrating a prompt digest an earlier record failed is refused; ACE-D5 recalibrates only after revision.
ACE-D2: the owner reads every objection the validation run returns, and an upheld one on anything amends the pair.

parts.statement: Every case has the required manifest fields.
Each detection statement is one sentence.
A harvested document's recorded source revision identifies its source.
Pair documents exist, are distinct and differ in one contiguous hunk; control-only cases have neither a defective document nor a site.
Evaluation cases never deploy.

obligations.source: ACE-D2: 'Cases live in src/user/.claude/skills/ac-attack/evals/, so they never deploy'; the manifest lists the ID, served parents, rule, lens, defect site, detection statement and harvested source revision; each case directory holds the prescribed documents.
obligations.statement: Deliver the prescribed case artifacts and manifest, while keeping evaluation cases out of deployment.

parts.statement: The case check refuses missing validation artifacts or documents differing from their recorded digests, and identifies the fault.
Before runs count, validation follows the required run and owner-review procedure, accepts the intended single defect, and resolves upheld additional defects.

obligations.source: ACE-D2: 'the owner validates a case before its runs count'; the owner reads the specified objections, confirms the planted defect and amends an upheld extra defect; control-only validation uses one whole panel run. The validation record contains the report, decision and document digests.
obligations.statement: Only substantively validated, unchanged cases contribute counted runs.

parts.statement: The catalogue contains the prescribed cases and rule coverage, with the prescribed parents, rules, lenses and child mappings; mismatches are identified.
Case documents actually instantiate the parent's specified defect and no-finding condition.
A committed catalogue passes the case check.

obligations.source: ACE-D3: 'A parent criterion's Given clause is its case's defect'; the no-finding clause is the correction or a feature outside the changed hunk; the case's lens is its rule's owner. The table specifies C1–C29 and P1.
obligations.statement: The catalogue implements ACE-D3's prescribed cases and their substantive parent scenarios.

parts.statement: Each counted run is a fresh dispatch.
Wrong transport, served model, effort, isolation or planned run count is refused with the difference named.
Transport unavailability cannot produce a completed evaluation through substituted or missing reports.

obligations.source: ACE-D4: 'A run is one fresh dispatch of one lens over one document.' ACE-D6 specifies transport, model, effort and Reads; substituted configurations do not count, and a down transport makes evaluation wait.
obligations.statement: Counted lens runs use fresh dispatches and the production configuration.

parts.statement: Detection follows the rule-and-site mechanical match and the specified judge-match alternatives, including site none.
A control is not silent only on an eligible objection matched by the judge to the detection statement.
Empty-control scoring uses lens reports of empty.
A P1 panel run passes only when all four lens runs contain no judge-confirmed demand for implementation criteria.

obligations.source: ACE-D4 defines mechanical and judged detection, judged control silence, empty reports and P1's four-lens panel-run pass condition.
obligations.statement: The scorer applies the specified detection, silence, emptiness and panel-run classifications.

parts.statement: Unusable reports after the allowed repeats and outstanding judgments contribute no rate, leave cases pending and report an incomplete evaluation.
No third repeat is planned, and repeats do not inflate the planned run count.

obligations.source: ACE-D4 permits at most two repeats for missing or wholly malformed reports; still-unusable reports or outstanding judgments leave the case pending, never scored as a miss.
obligations.statement: Missing usable reports or required judgments leave cases pending and the evaluation incomplete.

parts.statement: The judge executes as Claude Opus through the native Agent tool using evals/judge.md.
Judge inputs contain exactly the specified case information or P1 objection, without lens, model or arm information.
Scoring rejects inadequate, wrongly labelled or identity-mismatched calibration; revised prompts use new calibration items, and case-task calibration includes mechanical detections.
Recorded judge model IDs and prompt digests identify the actual judgment executions.
Compared lock sets use one judge model ID and one judge prompt digest.

obligations.source: ACE-D5 specifies Claude Opus through the native Agent tool with evals/judge.md, the case and P1 inputs, owner-labelled twenty-item calibration with eighteen agreements, new items after failed calibration, and resolved model and prompt-digest records.
obligations.statement: Judgments use the specified judge, calibrated tasks, minimal inputs and correctly recorded execution identity.

parts.statement: Initial attempts use the specified five runs per document, including four lens runs per P1 panel run.
Retested sides are judged on all ten runs, and usable reports correspond one to one with planned runs.

obligations.source: ACE-D7: 'An attempt plans five runs of each of its documents'; a permitted retest adds five runs, and 'No run is discarded.'
obligations.statement: Each attempt follows the fixed run-count and run-retention contract.

parts.statement: Detection passes at four or five of five and eight of ten, and fails at two of five and seven of ten.
Detection fails at zero or one of five and at the reachable retest totals three through six of ten.
Control silence passes at four or five of five and eight of ten, and fails at two of five and seven of ten.
Control silence fails at zero or one of five and at the reachable retest totals three through six of ten.
An initial side at three of five receives its one earned retest, including P1.
Retests are restricted to eligible three-of-five sides and are scored using all ten runs.
P1 locks at four or five passing panel runs of five.
P1 fails at zero through two of five, passes its earned retest at eight of ten, and fails that retest at three through seven of ten.

obligations.source: ACE-D7: four of five passes; three of five gets one retest and passes at eight of ten; below three fails; P1 uses the same retest.
obligations.statement: The scorer and planner implement all initial and retest threshold outcomes.

parts.statement: Pair locking requires both passing sides, parent acceptance requires every serving case locked, scoring uses planned thresholds, and case decisions do not average rates across cases.

obligations.source: ACE-D7: a pair locks when detection and control both hold; a parent passes only when every serving case locks; 'No rate is averaged across cases.' ACE-D7 also requires scoring under the plan's thresholds.
obligations.statement: Locking and parent acceptance follow the case-level contract rather than averages.

parts.statement: The scorer passes at 80 percent, fails below it and cannot pass without current-lock control runs.
Every production lens actually passes that rate in the evaluation of record.

obligations.source: ACE-D7: a lens passes ACQ-A27 at at least 80 percent empty control runs behind current locks, P1 included; this pooled rate earns no retest.
obligations.statement: Every lens meets the pooled empty-control threshold on its current locks.

parts.statement: An unapproved plan above 310 dispatches is refused and its count is named.

obligations.source: ACE-D7: the whole catalogue plans 310 dispatches; 'The planner refuses a larger plan, an experiment's plan included, unless the plan names the owner's approval.'
obligations.statement: Plans exceeding the approved default dispatch budget require named owner approval.

parts.statement: Scoring enforces the planned configuration, run correspondence and thresholds.
The complete plan is written and fixed before the first dispatch.
An already attempted fingerprint cannot be attempted again, regardless of its outcome.
A planned attempt without committed reports blocks another attempt and is identified.

obligations.source: ACE-D8: the planner writes a plan before dispatch, fixing every dispatch, configuration, thresholds and cases; it refuses another attempt on an attempted fingerprint and any new attempt while planned reports are uncommitted.
obligations.statement: Plans fix attempts in advance and prevent repeated attempts or overlapping uncommitted attempts.

parts.statement: A baseline attempt on every case is committed.
All other attempts and all their reports, including superseded repeat reports, are committed in the prescribed run archive.

obligations.source: ACE-D8: 'Every attempt is committed with its reports under evals/runs/<run-id>/, whatever it shows'; superseded repeat reports 'stay committed'. S2.6 requires a baseline attempt on every case.
obligations.statement: Attempt evidence is committed without outcome-based omissions.

parts.statement: The scorer reads the served model from transport response metadata rather than the plan.
Every report carries its transport response ID.
Usable reports match planned runs one to one, duplicate response IDs are refused, superseded reports match nothing, and offending runs or reports are named.

obligations.source: ACE-D8: each report carries the transport's served model and response ID; usable reports match planned runs one to one; duplicate response IDs are refused; superseded reports match nothing.
obligations.statement: Reports preserve transport identity and match the planned attempt without duplication.

parts.statement: Document or emitted-prompt changes void exactly the locks whose fingerprints change, with affected locks named.
Unchanged attempted fingerprints cannot be rerun when another case changes.

obligations.source: ACE-D8 defines pair and P1 prompt fingerprints, including emitted lens, template and rule content with production model and effort; changes void exactly the altered fingerprints and only those cases rerun.
obligations.statement: Locks remain current only for their producing prompts and configuration, with selective invalidation.

parts.statement: Changed judging or scoring rescores stored reports without planned lens dispatch and retains only still-passing locks.

obligations.source: ACE-D8: judge-prompt, judge-model or scorer changes dispatch no lens; stored reports are rescored and a lock stands only if its case still passes.
obligations.statement: Judge or scorer changes rescore stored evidence without new lens dispatches.

parts.statement: C1 holds a current lock.
C2 holds a current lock.
C3 holds a current lock.
C4 holds a current lock.
C5 holds a current lock.
C6 holds a current lock.
C7 holds a current lock.

C18 holds a current lock.

C24 holds a current lock.
C25 holds a current lock.
C26 holds a current lock.
C27 holds a current lock.
C28 holds a current lock.
C29 holds a current lock.
P1 holds a current lock.

obligations.source: ACE-D8: 'The evaluation of record is the set of current locks.' S2.7 'stays open until every case holds a current lock.' ACE-D3 maps every catalogue case to its child criterion.
obligations.statement: The evaluation of record contains current locks for the prescribed catalogue.

parts.statement: The report presents each lens's pooled detection and silence rates.
Comparison reports improves exactly for baseline-lock preservation and gains in at least two lenses, otherwise identifying the regression or missing gain.
Comparison refuses incompatible configurations, judge identities, case populations or pending evidence.

obligations.source: ACE-D7: 'The scorer also reports each lens's pooled rates, which decide nothing.' ACE-D9 defines improvement as retaining every baseline lock and gaining a locked case in at least two lenses.
obligations.statement: Comparison and reporting expose the prescribed evaluation outcomes.

parts.statement: Later registry entries carry reproducible improves reports from committed lock sets, with the later set covering the whole catalogue.
The first registry entry identifies the template as this spec originally finds it.
Each comparison's baseline and changed template digests match the preceding and current registry entries, establishing improvement against the template without the addition.
The current shared-template digest matches the registry's last entry.

obligations.source: ACE-D9: an addition ships only with a whole-catalogue improves comparison against the template without it; the registry begins with the template as found, and later entries record comparisons against their predecessors; the current digest is pinned to the last entry.
obligations.statement: Shared-template additions are authorized by a reproducible improvement chain from the original template.

parts.statement: The baseline attempt on every case is committed.
Each lens body receives mandates for the rules it gained.
A lens-level comparison is recorded for each revised lens.
Each revised lens's comparison demonstrates no case regression.

obligations.source: S2.6: 'A baseline attempt on every case, then body revisions for the rules each lens gained, each shown by a lens-level comparison to regress no case.'
obligations.statement: Lens mandates are revised using baseline evidence and comparisons demonstrating no case regression.

parts.statement: The verification child cannot close before every case has a current lock.

obligations.source: S2.7 describes the verification child and says: 'It stays open until every case holds a current lock.'
obligations.statement: Verification completion waits for the required current-lock evidence.

ground.reason: ACE-D2 requires validation before a case's runs count and requires amendment when the owner upholds an objection. ACE-A13 checks that the validation record contains a report, an owner's decision and matching digests. It does not require that the decision accepts the recorded documents.

objections.objection: ACE-A13 permits a case rejected by its owner to pass the case check because its rejection record has all the required fields.
objections.obligation: Only validated cases contribute evaluation runs.

scenario.expect: The case check passes while the owner's upheld objection remains unresolved and the pair has not been validated for evaluation.
scenario.given: A pair satisfies every structural requirement in ACE-A13. Its validation record contains the report, matching document digests and the owner's decision that an additional defect requires amendment. The documents remain unamended.
scenario.when: The case check applies ACE-A13.

ground.reason: The ordered S2.6 slice requires each revised lens to be 'shown by a lens-level comparison to regress no case'. Its continuation AC requires only 'a committed baseline attempt on every case, and a lens-level comparison per revised lens'. The existence of a comparison does not establish its required result.

objections.objection: The S2.6 continuation accepts comparisons that report regressions because it does not require a non-regression verdict.
objections.obligation: Each lens revision preserves every case locked under its baseline.

scenario.expect: The continuation's check passes because the baseline and comparisons exist, while a revised lens has lost a previously locked case.
scenario.given: A committed baseline attempt covers every case. Every revised lens has a comparison, and one comparison reports that a baseline-locked case fails under the revision.
scenario.when: S2.6 is assessed against its continuation AC.

ground.reason: ACE-D2 requires a 'one-sentence detection statement'. ACE-A13 checks whether the manifest field exists, without checking this content constraint.

objections.objection: A manifest can contain detection statements that violate the specified format.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although a detection statement contains several sentences.
scenario.given: A valid catalogue has a multi-sentence detection statement that the judge can match consistently.
scenario.when: The case check, evaluation and remaining checks run.

ground.reason: ACE-D2 requires 'the source revision of any harvested document'. Field presence under ACE-A13 does not establish that the revision identifies the harvested source.

objections.objection: A harvested case can carry incorrect source provenance.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although the recorded revision belongs to a different source document.
scenario.given: A harvested case has all manifest fields, valid document digests and passing evaluation results, but its source revision is incorrect.
scenario.when: The catalogue and evaluation checks run.

ground.reason: ACE-D2 says cases live under evals 'so they never deploy'. No criterion observes deployment exclusion.

objections.objection: Evaluation documents can be deployed with the production skill.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes while the installed skill contains evaluation cases.
scenario.given: The evaluation implementation passes its checks, but an installer change copies evals directories.
scenario.when: The criteria are checked and the skill is subsequently installed.

ground.reason: ACE-D2 requires the owner to validate the specified control run, read the relevant objections and amend a pair when an objection is upheld. ACE-A13 checks record presence and digests, without checking this decision or procedure.

objections.objection: Runs can count for a case that its owner has rejected or has not substantively validated.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although the owner upheld an additional defect and the pair was never amended.
scenario.given: A case has a validation report, matching digests and an owner decision rejecting the pair. Its later stochastic runs meet the lock thresholds.
scenario.when: The case check accepts the record and the evaluation counts those later runs.

ground.reason: ACE-D3 says a parent's Given clause supplies the defect and its no-finding clause is corrected or present outside the changed hunk. Metadata agreement and successful detection of a declared statement do not establish those document contents.

objections.objection: A case can obtain a lock while testing a different defect or omitting the parent's no-finding condition.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although a named parent claim has not been exercised by its prescribed case.
scenario.given: A pair has the correct table metadata and one changed hunk, but plants a different defect. Its detection statement describes that replacement defect, and its control omits the required no-finding feature.
scenario.when: The declared defect is detected sufficiently often and the case receives a current lock.

ground.reason: ACE-D4 defines a run as 'one fresh dispatch'. ACE-A18 checks configuration and isolation, and ACE-A53 checks report correspondence and response IDs. Neither checks dispatch freshness.

objections.objection: An evaluation can count responses generated within a reused conversation.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although the counted runs are not fresh dispatches.
scenario.given: A runner reuses one conversation while satisfying the specified transport, model, effort and read isolation. Every response has a distinct transport response ID.
scenario.when: It generates the planned reports and the scorer locks the cases.

ground.reason: ACE-D5 fixes the judge as 'Claude Opus through the native Agent tool' with evals/judge.md. The criteria check calibration and input content, without checking this execution configuration.

objections.objection: A calibrated substitute judge can satisfy the criteria.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although judgments are produced by a different model or transport.
scenario.given: A substitute judge reaches eighteen agreements in twenty, has matching calibration and run identifiers, and receives exactly the required input.
scenario.when: The scorer uses its judgments and completes the evaluation.

ground.reason: ACE-D5 requires the run record to name the judge's 'resolved model ID' and prompt digest. ACE-A20 and ACE-A23 establish agreement between recorded identifiers, without establishing their agreement with the execution.

objections.objection: Consistently incorrect judge identity records can pass the checks.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although the recorded judge model ID or prompt digest does not identify what actually ran.
scenario.given: Calibration and judgment runs use the required judge, but their records consistently contain the same incorrect model ID or prompt digest.
scenario.when: Calibration validation and lock-set comparisons check those records.

ground.reason: ACE-D7 says a side below three of five fails and a retested side passes at eight of ten. ACE-A15 explicitly checks failure at two of five and seven of ten, leaving the other reachable failing counts unrepresented.

objections.objection: The scorer can accept other failing detection counts while passing every specified scoring scenario.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but detection is accepted at one of five or six of ten.
scenario.given: The scorer handles four, five and two detections out of five, and eight and seven out of ten, as specified. It incorrectly accepts zero or one out of five and three through six out of ten. Actual catalogue attempts use covered passing counts.
scenario.when: The specified checks run, followed by scoring an attempt with an uncovered failing count.

ground.reason: ACE-D7 applies the same thresholds to control silence. ACE-A16 explicitly checks failure at two of five and seven of ten, leaving the other reachable failing counts unrepresented.

objections.objection: The scorer can accept other failing control counts while passing every specified scoring scenario.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes, but the control holds at one silent run of five or six of ten.
scenario.given: The scorer handles the counts named in ACE-A16 correctly. It incorrectly accepts zero or one silent run of five and three through six of ten. Actual catalogue attempts use covered passing counts.
scenario.when: The specified checks run, followed by scoring an attempt with an uncovered failing count.

ground.reason: ACE-D7 says a side at three of five 'gets one retest'. ACE-A46 permits retests only at that count, but does not require an eligible retest to be planned.

objections.objection: The planner can withhold an earned retest.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although an eligible side receives no retest.
scenario.given: The planner correctly restricts any retest it creates, but refuses to create one for a side at three of five. Recorded catalogue cases pass on their initial attempts.
scenario.when: The specified checks run and an additional attempt reaches three of five.

ground.reason: ACE-D7 gives P1 the same failure thresholds and retest. ACE-A51 checks individual panel runs, and ACE-A52 checks P1 locking at four or five passing panel runs of five. Neither checks P1's other reachable scoring outcomes.

objections.objection: P1's failure and retest scoring can be incorrect.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although P1 locks at two of five or fails to lock at eight of ten after its earned retest.
scenario.given: The scorer classifies each four-lens panel run correctly and locks P1 at four or five of five, but mishandles the remaining initial and retest counts. The evaluation of record uses five passing panel runs.
scenario.when: The specified checks run, followed by a P1 attempt exercising an omitted count.

ground.reason: ACE-D8 requires the planner to write the plan 'before any dispatch' and fix every dispatch, configuration, threshold and case. Checking correspondence to the final plan does not establish when it was fixed.

objections.objection: An operator can choose or amend the plan after seeing results.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although the evaluation plan was constructed or changed after dispatch.
scenario.given: Reports are generated first. A matching plan is then written with compliant configuration, counts and thresholds, before any new attempt is requested.
scenario.when: The scorer checks the completed plan and its corresponding reports.

ground.reason: ACE-D8 says every attempt is committed with its reports 'whatever it shows' and that superseded reports stay committed. ACE-A21 blocks a subsequent attempt; ACE-A53 checks report matching. Neither requires the final attempt and all its reports to be committed.

objections.objection: The evaluation of record can rely on uncommitted reports or omit superseded reports from git.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although the final attempt or its superseded reports are absent from committed history.
scenario.given: The required baseline and comparison lock sets are committed. A final attempt produces valid current locks, but its reports remain uncommitted, and no subsequent attempt is requested.
scenario.when: The evaluation-of-record checks run.

ground.reason: ACE-D8 says each report carries the transport's response ID. ACE-A53 forbids two reports sharing an ID, without explicitly requiring an ID on every report.

objections.objection: One usable report can lack its transport response ID.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although one report lacks the required response ID.
scenario.given: Reports match planned runs one to one using their run identities. All have correct model metadata, all present response IDs are unique, and exactly one report has no response ID.
scenario.when: The scorer validates and scores the attempt.

ground.reason: ACE-D9 requires the registry's first entry to be 'the template as this spec finds it'. ACE-A24 checks the current digest against the last entry and comparisons after the first, without pinning the first entry.

objections.objection: A changed template can be substituted for the initial registry baseline.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although an addition ships without comparison against the original template.
scenario.given: The template is changed and a one-entry registry is initialized with the changed digest. All catalogue cases obtain current locks.
scenario.when: The emitter suite checks the current digest and finds no later registry entry requiring comparison evidence.

ground.reason: ACE-D9 requires each later entry's comparison to be against the entry before it, and an addition to be evaluated against the template without it. ACE-A24 requires reproducible improving lock sets, without explicitly binding their template digests to the adjacent registry entries.

objections.objection: An unrelated improving comparison can authorize a template addition.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although the current template has no improving comparison against its predecessor.
scenario.given: The registry has correct predecessor and current template digests. Its later entry names committed whole-catalogue lock sets whose genuine improving comparison evaluates different template versions.
scenario.when: The comparison reproduces that report and the emitter suite checks the registry.

ground.reason: S2.6 promises 'body revisions for the rules each lens gained'. Passing fixed cases and recording a comparison do not establish that those rules were added to the lens bodies.

objections.objection: The catalogue can pass while required lens mandates remain absent.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although a lens body omits a rule it was supposed to gain.
scenario.given: The model detects the fixed planted defects without an explicit mandate for the gained rule. Baseline attempts and the required comparisons are committed.
scenario.when: Every case obtains a current lock and the continuation checks run.

ground.reason: S2.6 requires each revised lens to be 'shown by a lens-level comparison to regress no case'. Its continuation requires a comparison to exist, without requiring a no-regression result.

objections.objection: A revised lens can ship with a recorded regression.

scenario.expect: Every criterion passes although a revised lens's comparison reports a regressed case.
scenario.given: A lens comparison is committed and reports a regression. A subsequent permitted prompt change produces current locks for the whole catalogue. No template addition invokes the shared-template gate.
scenario.when: The final evaluation and the continuation requiring a comparison per revised lens are checked.

ground.reason: S2.7 says the verification child 'stays open until every case holds a current lock'. Final lock checks do not observe whether the child was closed prematurely.

objections.objection: The verification child can close before its required evidence exists.

scenario.expect: Every criterion eventually passes despite the verification child having closed while cases were still unlocked.
scenario.given: The verification child is closed before evaluation completes.
scenario.when: Later runs obtain all current locks and the final criteria are checked.

ground.reason: The continuations repeatedly require 'make content-tests exits 0'. Outside the acceptance criteria, the document promises particular suites and behavior, but does not separately promise this gate's exit status. Exit status alone establishes none of those substantive obligations.

objections.objection: The additional gate criterion discharges no inventoried obligation. Its artifact-level obligation needs an explicit basis if it is to remain.

scenario.expect: The gate's exit-status check runs while no independently stated document obligation depends on that status itself.
scenario.given: The named behavioral and catalogue criteria are checked independently.
scenario.when: The additional continuation check observes whether make content-tests exits 0.

ground.reason: ACE-D7 folds P1 into each lens's pooled empty-control rate for ACQ-A27, but ACE-D4 defines 'control run' and 'empty' only for single-lens runs over a control document, and P1's runs are full-panel runs judged by a different rule; the wording never says which P1 runs enter which lens's denominator or what 'empty' means for a panel run.

objections.objection: The ACQ-A27 pass/fail verdict for a lens flips at the 80-percent boundary depending on whether P1's panel runs count in that lens's rate, so ACE-A17 and ACE-A43 admit opposite verdicts on the same runs.

scenario.expect: counting P1's runs gives 60/80 = 75% and the lens fails; excluding them gives 60/75 = 80% and the lens passes — one run set, two verdicts
scenario.given: behavioural-outcome holds current locks on its 15 pair cases (75 control runs, exactly 60 of them empty) and on P1, whose five behavioural-outcome runs each raised an objection the judge cleared, so none reports `empty`
scenario.when: the scorer judges ACE-A17 and ACE-A43

ground.reason: ACE-D8 has the plan written before any dispatch fixing every dispatch, ACE-A46 has the planner plan a retest only after a side lands at three of five, and ACE-A53 refuses an attempt whose usable reports do not match its planned runs one to one; whether the retest's five runs are 'planned runs' is left open.

objections.objection: A retested side either can never be scored (its ten reports exceed the five planned runs, so ACE-A53 refuses the attempt) or scores normally at eight of ten, depending on how 'the plan fixes every dispatch' is read.
objections.obligation: ACE-D8's plan-fixing rule against ACE-A46's retest planning and ACE-A53's one-to-one match

scenario.expect: under one reading the ten usable reports do not match the five planned runs and the attempt is refused (no 3/5 side ever locks); under the other the retest runs are planned and the side passes at eight of ten
scenario.given: an attempt whose pre-dispatch plan lists five runs per document for a case, and a side that lands at exactly three of five
scenario.when: the planner plans the earned retest, five more runs are committed, and the scorer applies ACE-A53

ground.reason: What if something it relies on is missing? ACE-A20 lists three refusal grounds for a calibration record — fewer than eighteen agreements, a wrong prompt digest or model ID, a wrong labeller — and ACE-A56 adds two more, but every ground assumes a record exists. No criterion tests a judgment task whose calibration record is entirely absent, so the scorer's behaviour on the missing-dependency case is undefined.

objections.objection: A judgment task with no calibration record at all falls through every enumerated refusal ground, and no criterion says the scorer refuses to score it.
objections.obligation: A judgment task counts only after calibration (ACE-D5)

scenario.expect: The scorer refuses to score the task, naming the missing calibration — ACE-D5 says a judgment task counts only after calibration — but ACE-A20 and ACE-A56 test only malformed records, never an absent one.
scenario.given: A run holding an objection owed a judgment, and no calibration record on disk for the judge prompt digest and judge model ID the run names
scenario.when: The scorer scores the attempt and reaches the judgment task

ground.reason: What if it runs again with nothing changed? ACE-A56 refuses only a calibration record that shares an item with a failed calibration of an earlier prompt digest. A failed calibration of the same prompt digest is not an earlier digest, so nothing stops re-labelling twenty fresh items against the unchanged judge prompt until one attempt reaches eighteen agreements — calibration shopping, which ACE-D8's one-attempt-per-fingerprint philosophy forbids for cases but no criterion forbids for the judge.

objections.objection: A judge prompt that failed calibration can be recalibrated unchanged until it passes, and the criteria neither refuse the second calibration nor rule the practice out.
objections.obligation: A prompt revised after a failed calibration is calibrated on twenty new items (ACE-D5)

scenario.expect: The scorer refuses the second calibration, as it would for a shared item under ACE-A56 — but ACE-A56 keys on an earlier prompt digest, and a repeated digest is the same digest, so the recalibrated judge scores runs.
scenario.given: A failed calibration record for judge prompt digest D, then a second calibration record for the same digest D over twenty disjoint items showing eighteen agreements
scenario.when: The owner submits the second calibration and the scorer scores a judgment task calibrated under it

ground.reason: What if it fails? ACE-D2's validation has the owner read only objections citing the case's rule or its site, and ACE-A13 checks the validation record's presence and digests, not what the run surfaced. A control carrying a second defect under a different rule produces an objection outside that reading scope, the pair validates anyway, and every later control-side lock rests on a control that is not defect-free. No criterion tests this failure path of validation.

objections.objection: A control document with an authored defect under a rule other than the case's own passes validation, because the owner never reads the objection that would expose it and the case check reads only the record's shape.
objections.obligation: The owner validates a case before its runs count (ACE-D2)

scenario.expect: Validation surfaces the objection and the pair is amended, since the pair then carries more than its one defect — but the reading scope in ACE-D2 excludes the objection, and ACE-A13 tests only that the record holds a report, a decision and digests.
scenario.given: A pair case whose control.md carries an authored defect covered by a rule other than the case's rule
scenario.when: The validation run over the control emits an objection citing that other rule, and the owner reads only objections citing the case's rule or site
